reports.headline: HBO Max fills November with cinema: 'Jojo Rabbit', 'The Whale' and 'Black Swan' on the 5th, 'Tres de más' on the 20th
reports.deck: HBO Max's Spanish catalogue announces a batch of films for November with specific dates, plus several European original series.
paragraphs: According to the calendar published by AVPasión (updated Wednesday 28), 'Jojo Rabbit' (Taika Waititi), 'The Whale' and 'Black Swan' (Darren Aronofsky) reach HBO Max in Spain on 5 November, together with 'Constantine' and 'The Color of Money'. On the 12th come 'Dangerous Minds', 'Contact' and 'Little Miss Sunshine', and on the 26th 'Locura padre' and 'El soldado de Dios'. These are platform dates for Spain; the articles consulted do not give years or directors for every title.

The Spanish comedy 'Tres de más' arrives on the 20th after its theatrical run. On the series side, Que.es lists 'The Gilded Age' (season 4) on 2 November, the Italian 'Melania Rea' on the 6th, 'Ciudad de Dios: La lucha no para' on the 8th and the thriller 'Infamia' on the 13th; the same day also lists two European productions, the Polish 'Silent Night' and the Hungarian 'Maniacs of Truth', without further details. 'The Good Daughter', an adaptation of a Karin Slaughter novel, appears on the 12th.

Why it matters: for this reader's profile, the interest is the November cycle with 'Black Swan' (psychological horror) and 'Jojo Rabbit' (period satire) on the same date, plus the curiosity of the two Eastern European series. Editorial affinity 3/5, medium confidence (not a critics' score). Both sources are non-official specialist press: check the platform.

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: National Theatre at Home schedules Stoppard's 'Arcadia' for 26 November and 'The Playboy of the Western World' for 1 December
reports.deck: The British theatre streaming catalogue lines up two classics before year's end, after 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses' (3 November).
paragraphs: The 'Coming soon' page of National Theatre at Home lists, besides 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses' (3 November, directed by Marianne Elliott), Tom Stoppard's 'Arcadia', directed by Carrie Cracknell and produced by the Old Vic, arriving on 26 November. On 1 December comes John Millington Synge's 'The Playboy of the Western World', directed by Caitríona McLaughlin with Nicola Coughlan, Éanna Hardwicke and Siobhán McSweeney.

Also scheduled are 'Kinky Boots' (1 December), 'A Child's Christmas in Wales' (8 December) and, for March 2027, 'Owain & Henry'. The service offers monthly or annual subscriptions, rentals and a one-week free trial, but the page does not say which model applies to each play, nor the recording year or subtitles.

Because the recording year, subtitles and exact access from Spain are missing, no full-recording card is given here: this is a calendar notice. Editorial affinity 4/5 for 'Arcadia', medium confidence (the recording has not been seen).

reports.headline: Seminci closes on Saturday with 'Hombre al agua', Gael García Bernal's comedy about class and masculinity
reports.deck: The 71st Valladolid festival ends on 31 October with the Mexican actor's third film as a director, which he also wrote and stars in.
paragraphs: According to Seminci's press release, 'Hombre al agua' is the closing film of the edition, held from 23 to 31 October. It is Gael García Bernal's third feature as a director; he wrote it and plays Camilo, a Cuban lifeguard who saves a Mexican businessman. The cast also includes Esmeralda Pimentel, Débora Nascimento, Natalia Oreiro and Ricky Martin.

The festival opened with Lili Horvát's 'My Notes on Mars', in the Official Section with Mackenzie Davis and Rupert Friend. The release notes that this will be Bernal's first visit to Valladolid, although two of his films have played there before: 'Museo' (2018) and 'Magallanes' (2025).

Why it matters: the Official Section results, with the Espiga de Oro, are due this Saturday the 31st; the release is dated 5 October and does not confirm the time or a commercial release date in Spain for 'Hombre al agua'. We have not seen the film. Editorial affinity 3/5, low confidence (social comedy; not a critics' score).

reports.headline: Calendar: Seminci results on Saturday, 'The Gilded Age' on HBO Max on 2 November and 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses' on the 3rd
reports.deck: Dates with territory for the coming weeks, only those found in this edition's sources.
paragraphs: 31 October (Spain): Seminci closes with 'Hombre al agua' and the 71st edition's results. 2 November (Spain, HBO Max): season four of 'The Gilded Age'. 3 November (National Theatre at Home): 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'.
5 November (Spain, HBO Max): 'Jojo Rabbit', 'The Whale' and 'Black Swan'. 13 November (Spain, HBO Max): the series 'Infamia'. 20 November (Spain, HBO Max): 'Tres de más'.
26 November (National Theatre at Home): 'Arcadia'. 1 December: 'The Playboy of the Western World' and 'Kinky Boots'. Platform dates can change; confirm them with the service.

reports.subject: film
reports.headline: Editor's picks: 'Black Swan' on 5 November, 'Arcadia' at the National Theatre and Seminci's closing night
reports.deck: Three suggestions for this late-October moment, with editorial affinity (not the critics' score).
paragraphs: 1) 'Black Swan' (2010, Darren Aronofsky), on HBO Max Spain on 5 November: psychological horror with ballet in the background; affinity 4/5, high confidence for the genre, though it is already a well-known film. 2) 'Arcadia' by Tom Stoppard, on National Theatre at Home on 26 November: a drama of ideas and relationships; affinity 4/5, medium confidence (the recording has not been seen). 3) 'Hombre al agua' by Gael García Bernal, at Seminci's closing on the 31st: social comedy; affinity 3/5, low confidence.
Day's wrap-up: a short edition because today's search found few verifiable news items; we preferred fewer reports to adding unconfirmed rumours.
